chapters.title: Away from the Presence of the LORD
chapters.html:
Jonah 1

Jonah Flees

1The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai, saying,

2"Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and call out against it, for their evil has come up before Me."

3Jonah rose to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid its fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.

The Storm

4But the LORD hurled a great wind onto the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship thought it would break apart.

5The mariners were afraid, and each cried out to his god, and they hurled the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for them. But Jonah had gone down into the inner part of the vessel, and had lain down and fallen fast asleep.

6The captain came to him and said to him, "What are you doing asleep? Rise, call to your God! Perhaps God will give a thought to us, and we will not perish."

7They said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this evil has come to us." They cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

8They said to him, "Tell us, please, you on whose account this evil has come to us: What is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? From what people are you?"

9He said to them, "I am a Hebrew, and I fear the LORD, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry ground."

10Then the men were greatly afraid, and said to him, "What is this you have done?" For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.

11They said to him, "What shall we do to you, so that the sea will quiet down for us?" For the sea was growing more and more stormy.

12He said to them, "Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will quiet down for you; for I know that it is because of me that this great storm has come upon you."

13The men rowed hard to bring the ship back to the dry ground, but they could not, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.

14Then they called to the LORD and said, "Please, LORD, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not lay innocent blood on us; for You, LORD, have done as You pleased."

15They picked up Jonah and hurled him into the sea, and the sea ceased from its rage.

16Then the men greatly feared the LORD; they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.

17The LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

Notes

  • v1 "Jonah son of Amittai" — the prophet of Jeroboam's day, His servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet, who was from Gath-hepher (2 Kings 14:25), who foretold Israel's border restored. Yonah is the word dove, as in He sent out the dove (Genesis 8:8), and Hosea's Ephraim has become like a dove, silly and without sense (Hosea 7:11). Amittai has the letters of emet, truth. In the Hebrew text v17 is 2:1, and the Greek follows the Hebrew; the English numbering is followed.

  • v2 "Nineveh, the great city… their evil has come up before Me" — the great city are the words of Genesis, where Asshur built Nineveh… that is the great city (Genesis 10:11–12). The evil that has come up is the outcry of Sodom, her outcry that has come to Me (Genesis 18:21); the Greek has the cry of its evil has come up to Me. Gadol, great, is the book's word: a great city, a great wind, a great storm (v4), great fear (vv10, 16), a great fish (v17).

  • vv3, 5 "away from the presence of the LORD… went down to Joppa… went down into it… had gone down" — mi-lifnei YHWH, word for word from before the face of the LORD, the words of Cain, who went out from before the face of the LORD (Genesis 4:16). Jonah sets off for Tarshish instead, the land of silver… brought from Tarshish (Jeremiah 10:9). And at each step va-yered, he went down: to Joppa, the port of the cedar rafts (2 Chronicles 2:16), into the ship, into its inner part, and asleep, va-yeradam, a word that sounds like it. The descent goes on into the sea (2:6).

  • vv4–5 "the LORD hurled a great wind… the ship thought it would break apart… they hurled the cargo" — hetil, hurl, four times: the LORD hurls the wind (v4), the mariners the cargo (v5), Jonah asks to be hurled (v12), and they hurl him (v15). Chishvah le-hishaver, word for word the ship thought to be broken: the ship is given a thought, as the captain hopes God will give one (v6). Nirdam, fast asleep, is Sisera's sleep, He was fast asleep and exhausted (Judges 4:21).

  • v6 "Rise, call to your God!" — qum qera, the same two words the LORD spoke in v2, Rise… call out: a foreign captain says to the prophet what God said to him. Yit'ashet, will give a thought, is found only here in the Hebrew Bible. Ve-lo noved, and we will not perish, is said again by the sailors (v14) and by the king of Nineveh (3:9).

  • vv7–10 "on whose account this evil has come to us… I fear the LORD… What is this you have done?" — ra'ah, evil, is the word of v2: Nineveh's evil came up before God, and now an evil comes down on the ship. The lot is the LORD's way of finding the one, as in the tribe that the LORD takes (Joshua 7:14). The four questions come in a rush; Jonah answers the last, and adds whom he fears. Ivri, a Hebrew: the Greek has a servant of the Lord, eved, nearly the same letters. Who made the sea and the dry ground names the God of let the dry ground be seen (Genesis 1:9), and Jonah has fled from Him onto the sea. What is this you have done? is God's question to the woman in the garden (Genesis 3:13), now asked by the sailors.

  • vv10, 16 "the men were greatly afraid… the men greatly feared the LORD" — va-yir'u… yir'ah gedolah, word for word they feared a great fear, twice, and the doubling is the plain greatly in English. Their fear grows: they were afraid of the storm (v5); they greatly feared when they learned whose storm it was (v10); and last they greatly feared the LORD (v16), with sacrifice and vows. Jonah says I fear the LORD (v9); the sailors are the ones who do.

  • vv13–15 "The men rowed hard… do not lay innocent blood on us… the sea ceased from its rage" — va-yachteru, rowed hard, word for word dug, the verb of dig through the wall (Ezekiel 8:8). Dam naqi, innocent blood, the law's word (Deuteronomy 19:10). Ka'asher chafatsta asita, You have done as You pleased, is what the psalm says of the LORD, He does whatever He pleases (Psalm 115:3). Za'af, rage, is the word of I will bear the rage of the LORD (Micah 7:9). The sailors' story is Psalm 107's, Some went down to the sea in ships… He made the storm a whisper (Psalm 107:23, 29).

  • v17 "The LORD appointed a great fish… three days and three nights" — va-yeman, appointed, God's verb four times in the book: the fish, the plant (4:6), the worm (4:7) and the east wind (4:8). Dag, fish; the Greek has ketos, a great sea creature, and so does Matthew, in Jesus' words: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea creature three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights (Matthew 12:40).

chapters.title: Out of the Belly of Sheol
chapters.html:
Jonah 2

Jonah's Prayer

1Then Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish,

2and said:
"I called out of my distress to the LORD,
and He answered me;
out of the belly of Sheol I cried for help,
and You heard my voice.

3You cast me into the depths,
into the heart of the seas,
and the current swirled around me;
all Your breakers and Your waves
have gone over me.

4I said, 'I am driven away
from before Your eyes;
yet I will look again
toward Your holy temple.'

5The waters surrounded me up to my neck;
the deep swirled around me;
reeds were wrapped around my head.

6I went down to the roots of the mountains;
the earth, its bars were behind me forever.
Yet You brought up my life from the pit,
LORD my God.

7When my soul grew faint within me,
I remembered the LORD,
and my prayer came to You,
to Your holy temple.

8Those who hold to empty idols
forsake their loyal love.

9But I, with the sound of thanksgiving,
will sacrifice to You;
what I have vowed I will pay.
Salvation belongs to the LORD!"

10The LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry ground.

Notes

  • v1 "from the belly of the fish" — in the Hebrew text vv1–10 are 2:2–11, and the Greek follows the Hebrew; the English numbering is followed. In this verse alone the fish is dagah, a feminine form; it is dag in 1:17 and 2:10. Me'ei, belly, is the inward parts, as in from your inward parts (Genesis 25:23).

  • v2 "I called out of my distress to the LORD, and He answered me… You heard my voice" — the prayer is made of the psalms. The first line is In my distress I called to the LORD, and He answered me (Psalm 120:1), and the second has the words of to my God I cried for help. From His temple He heard my voice (Psalm 18:6). Mi-beten She'ol, out of the belly of Sheol, uses beten, the word for belly and womb, as in Two nations are in your belly (Genesis 25:23).

  • v3 "You cast me into the depths… all Your breakers and Your waves have gone over me" — the sailors hurled him (1:15), but Jonah says You cast me. Tashlikheni metsulah, You cast me into the depths, is the verb and noun of Micah's hope, You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea (Micah 7:19), and of the Egyptians who went down into the depths like a stone (Exodus 15:5). The last line is word for word the psalm's, all Your breakers and Your waves have gone over me (Psalm 42:7). Bi-levav yammim, into the heart of the seas, is where the ship of Tyre sank (Ezekiel 27:26).

  • v4 "I am driven away from before Your eyes; yet I will look again toward Your holy temple" — the psalm says I am cut off from before Your eyes (Psalm 31:22); nigrashti, driven away, has nearly the letters of its nigrazti, cut off, and is the verb of Cain, You have driven me out this day (Genesis 4:14). Akh, yet, makes the second line a hope; the Greek reads it as a question, shall I look again toward Your holy temple?

  • vv5–6 "The waters surrounded me up to my neck… reeds were wrapped around my head… I went down to the roots of the mountains" — ad nefesh, up to my neck, as in the waters have come up to my neck (Psalm 69:1), and afafuni, surrounded me, as in The cords of death surrounded me (Psalm 18:4). Tehom, the deep, is the deep of darkness lay over the face of the deep (Genesis 1:2). Suf, reeds, are the reeds of the Sea of Reeds (Exodus 15:4). Yaradti, I went down, is the last step of the descent of chapter 1 (1:3, 5), down to the roots of the mountains.

  • vv6–7 "Yet You brought up my life from the pit… When my soul grew faint within me, I remembered the LORD" — va-ta'al, You brought up, the turn of the prayer, as in You brought up my soul from Sheol; You kept me alive, so that I did not go down to the pit (Psalm 30:3), and shachat, the pit, as in who redeems your life from the pit (Psalm 103:4). Be-hit'attef alai nafshi, when my soul grew faint within me, is the psalm's When my spirit grows faint within me with soul for spirit (Psalm 142:3), and my prayer came to You answers Let my prayer come before You (Psalm 88:2).

  • v8 "Those who hold to empty idols forsake their loyal love" — meshammerim havlei shav are nearly the words of I hate those who hold to empty idols (Psalm 31:6). Chasdam, their loyal love, may be the chesed they themselves owe, or the LORD, the one who gives it, whom they leave. The Greek has their mercy. Spoken from the fish, the line stands beside chapter 1, where the men who once cried each to his god (1:5) left their gods and greatly feared the LORD (1:16).

  • v9 "with the sound of thanksgiving… what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD!" — be-qol todah, with the sound of thanksgiving, as in to make the sound of thanksgiving heard (Psalm 26:7); what I have vowed I will pay, as I will pay my vows to the LORD (Psalm 116:14). The sailors made vows on deck (1:16); Jonah makes his in the fish. The last words are the psalm's, Salvation belongs to the LORD (Psalm 3:8).

  • v10 "it vomited Jonah out onto the dry ground" — va-yaqe, vomited out, is the land's verb in the law, it will vomit you out (Leviticus 18:28). Ha-yabbashah, the dry ground, is what the LORD made (1:9) and what the sailors could not reach (1:13).
